title: Big Tech Stock Prices
text:
This dataset contains daily stock prices and trading volume for 14 large tech companies from 2010 to 2023. The line plot below represents the adjusted closing prices for Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Amazon, household tech names with large market capitalizations (the stock prices for these four companies were recorded on 12/29/2022 at the latest). Adjusted closing price is the closing price adjusted for stock splits and dividends issued, so that stock prices can be accurately compared across the observed time frame.


Code
library(tidyverse)

big_tech_stock_prices <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2023/2023-02-07/big_tech_stock_prices.csv')

big_tech_stock_prices |>
    filter(stock_symbol == "AAPL" | stock_symbol == "MSFT" | stock_symbol == "NVDA" | stock_symbol == "AMZN") |>
    ggplot(aes(x = date, y = adj_close, color = stock_symbol)) + 
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.4) +
    labs(x = "Date", y = "Adjusted close price (USD)", color = "Ticker", title = "Adjusted closing price, 2010 to 2022")









Data source: TidyTuesday, February 7, 2023.
Original data: Evan Gower compiled the data in 2023. The Big Tech Stock Prices data set comes from Yahoo Finance and was obtained through Kaggle.

title: NFL Attendance
text:
This dataset records weekly and season-total attendance for every NFL team from 2000 to 2019. The plot shows total league attendance by season.


Code
library(tidyverse)

attendance <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2020/2020-02-04/attendance.csv')

attendance |>
    group_by(year) |>
    summarize(league_total = sum(weekly_attendance, na.rm = TRUE) / 2) |> #The data set reports each game's weekly attendance twice, one time for each team that played, so the weekly total attendances are divided by two.
    ggplot(aes(x = year, y = league_total / 1000000)) +
    geom_line() +
    geom_point() +
    labs(x = "Season", y = "Total attendance (millions)", title = "NFL total attendance by season, 2000 to 2019")









Data source: TidyTuesday, February 4, 2020.
Original data: The data comes from the Pro Football Reference website, published by Sports Reference LLC. Each individual year was obtained from each year’s NFL attendance page; see 2019’s attendance data here.
